Anya D: quick sync — ran the sustained qps test for OrionPay POC across two AZs. attaching quick notes below.
Matt S: nice, what profile did you use?
Anya D: 30m run, 3 client workers per AZ, target 150 qps total (75 qps/az), 8k token avg request, caching enabled for repeated prefixes. Locust scenario: steady ramp to 150 qps in 90s, hold 30m, then 60s ramp down.
Tim E: good. what infra were we on? instance types, model, quantization?
Anya D: Dedicated pool: 4x A100-80GB (1 pool spanning both AZs via routing), model = rw-large-v2 (int8-opt), batcher config = auto-batch 8ms max delay, KV cache warm enabled. Canary policy set to 10%.
Julie (SE): summary numbers? p50/p95/p99? tail behavior?
Anya D: aggregated across AZs: p50 = 58ms, p95 = 230ms, p99 = 520ms. 99.9th spikes to ~1.2s during a cache eviction event at +22min. CPU/GPU utilization steady ~68% on serving nodes.
Matt S: 520ms p99 is higher than their target (<= 350ms). any obvious root cause?
Anya D: two contributors: 1) KV cache eviction + refill pattern when worker restart coincided with a small GC in the runtime, 2) rare long tails from prefix compaction when sequence length jumped (some requests had 4x token length).
Tim E: can we mitigate quickly for the POC next run?
Anya D: yes — short-term: bump cache size by 25%, increase async prefetch window to reduce miss penalty, and add a small prioritized fast-path for requests under 2k tokens. Also reduce max batching delay from 8ms -> 4ms (slight throughput hit, better tail).
Julie (SE): if we apply that, do you expect p99 to drop under 350ms?
Anya D: estimate: p50 ~60ms, p95 ~180ms, p99 ~300ms in the next run (still depends on token-length mix). Also rerun with a synthetic token-length distribution that matches OrionPay's real traces — we asked them for a sample yesterday.
Matt S: cost/throughput note for the CRO: running dedicated pool as above is approx $12.50/hr for the reserved pool (amortized), with ~0.9M tokens/min at 150 qps. If they prefer hosted, cost delta ~+30% but simpler infra.
Tim E: security blocker — OrionPay has a section in their questionnaire asking for KMS/HSM key lineage and per-customer key control for Private. Are we ok to commit for the POC?
Julie (SE): we can demo KMS envelope encryption for the POC, but full HSM-backed key custody needs enterprise contract. For evaluation we can provide logs showing CMEK integration and audit trails.
Anya D: onboarding note: they also asked about cross-AZ failover — we tested routing fallback: when we drained AZ-b, traffic shifted within 2s and p50 stayed within 10% but p99 increased ~40% for ~90s as caches warmed. That matches expectations and is safe for their SLA if they provision ~20% headroom.
OpsBot: deploy started: rollout id=rollout-2134506789, canary=10%, target pool=dedicated-orion-4, config=cache+bump, batching=4ms
DeployBot: load test runner started at 2134507000, locust scenario id=locust-orpoc-031
Matt S: next actions — 1) schedule re-run with the cache/batching fixes and OrionPay token distribution (waiting on their sample), 2) produce a one-pager showing the p99 improvement and cost delta, 3) confirm KMS demo artifacts for their security team.
Anya D: agreed. ETA for rerun + one-pager: end of day tomorrow if we get the token sample today.
Julie (SE): I'll draft the one-pager and include a short appendix with the exact locust commands and config snippet.
Anya D: locust command we used: ```locust -f locustfile.py --headless -u 450 -r 5 --run-time 30m --csv=orion-run```
Anya D: config snippet we changed: ```batching.max_delay_ms=4
cache.kv_size=32768
prefetch.window=48```
Matt S: pinging OrionPay for trace sample now. I'll also add a short note about expected cost for hosted vs dedicated.
Tim E: once we have the rerun, let's gate any enterprise commitment on passing p99 <=350ms for their exact trace. If not, propose a small architectural tweak (shard-by-customer cache) and estimate impact.
Anya D: noted. anything else?
Julie (SE): security will want the CMEK demo doc — I'll attach in the one-pager.
Anya D: thanks all — will post results after tomorrow's run. :thumbsup:
Matt S: thanks team.
Tim E: thanks.
